courier-relay/protocol-negotiation: courier-relay/protocol-negotiation: Request protocol resolution and error contract. An omitted "protocol" field selects CURRENT_PROTOCOL ("2" as of trial-1y9, the provider's permanently-adopted protocol approved by the integration owner). An explicit protocol value not in the supported set returns {"error": "unsupported_protocol"} (no other fields), matching the style of the existing {"error": "unknown_command"} response for unrecognized commands (inferred-but-reasonable extension of the spec text; established in trial-bk7, unchanged since). Protocol "1" remains supported for explicit requests per the AGENTS.md contract that explicit versions remain supported after a new current version is introduced; SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS is {"1","2"}. Protocol 1 identifies a delivery by delivery_id alone; protocol 2 identifies a delivery by the (account_id, delivery_id) pair (same delivery_id under a different account is a separate delivery), per the provider's delivery-ID allocation guarantee (vendor/protocol-1.md; trial-1y9 description). Representative-selection rule DIFFERS by protocol: protocol 1 accepts the receipt with the EARLIEST occurred_at UTC instant per identity (per vendor/protocol-1.md, the original provider contract); protocol 2 accepts the LATEST occurred_at UTC instant per identity (per the trial-1y9 contract text). Both tie-break equal instants by smallest record_id. This corrects an error in the prior version of this record, which stated both protocols use latest-instant selection; verified in trial-0my by reading vendor/protocol-1.md directly and confirming main.py select_winners() now branches earliest-vs-latest on protocol. Response shape for count/summary is {"protocol","accepted_count","duplicate_count"}; accepted (trial-vr3, extended to protocol 1 in trial-0my) adds a "receipts" array of the accepted representatives in original input order, unchanged; shape is unchanged across protocols. When a future protocol becomes current, add its value to SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS and update CURRENT_PROTOCOL in main.py, keep prior protocol values (and their own identity/selection/tie-break rules, which may differ per protocol as protocols 1 and 2 already do) supported, and archive the prior version of this record under a historical key (see courier-relay/protocol-negotiation-as-of-trial-bk7 for the pre-protocol-2 state) before overwriting it.
